data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 asserts necessity too strongly and then undercuts it via its own counterconditions: if a strong adversarial persona or high-temperature sampling can force the engine into low-probability latent regions that depart from the high-probability manifold used at authoring, then the same model has reached a 'collision of different priors' without a separate engine. SRC_003 gives no reason to believe adversarial prompting cannot replicate that collision, so the necessity claim ('genuine verification requires different priors; without a separate engine...') is not established and fails the standard.
